**Finding submitted: `missing` (critical, ip-data).**

**What I found**

- The MSA has no intellectual property or data ownership article at all. The only proprietary-rights language is:
  - § 6(a) (p0025) — allocates *liability* for the Content and Properties to AP ("responsible and solely liable for all the Content (including… all intellectual property rights therein)"), but says nothing about *ownership*.
  - § 14(b) (p0065) — covers names, trademarks and logos only.
  - § 2 (p0002) — a revocable, limited licence *to* AP for the Auction Platform; § 9(b)(vii)–(viii) confirm only Kubient's ownership of the Service and Platform.
- Nothing confirms AP retains rights in its Content, Properties, Inventory, Requests or the visitor/user data Kubient collects, measures and stores under § 9(b)(iii) — a real gap given the aggregated-data value in ad-tech deals.
- Nothing addresses deliverables/reports Kubient produces for AP, and there is no licence-back for Kubient IP embedded in them.
- Importantly, no clause assigns AP IP or data to Kubient and no joint ownership is created, so this is a gap rather than a walk-away trigger.

**Redline (validated, `ok:true`)** — one new § 6(b) inserted after p0025: AP owns Content, Properties, Inventory, Requests and all Customer Data; Kubient retains the Auction Platform and its pre-existing tools and know-how; Kubient assigns deliverables created for AP and grants a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence to any embedded Kubient IP; Kubient gets only a limited licence to use Customer Data to deliver the Services; no joint ownership.

The comment offers the fallback (perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence to deliverables instead of assignment) if Kubient resists the assignment mechanic.
